newsitem.title: UK: Europe's direct insurers to build on motor - report.
newsitem.headline: Europe's direct insurers to build on motor - report.

text.p: Direct, or telephone, insurance companies in Europe will use their success in breaking into motor insurance to diversify into other areas, management consultancy Datamonitor said.

"The success of telephone sales of motor insurance has been the spring-board for diversification for many providers," Datamonitor said on Monday, adding that the direct market is set for strong growth in the next five years.

The UK and the Netherlands account for 80 percent of insurance sold over the telephone in Europe, with 60 percent of total European direct sales being motor insurance, the report, 'European Tele-Insurance: A Promise Unfulfilled', said.
Datamonitor estimates the total value of the European personal non-life insurance market at $151.8 billion, with direct accounting for $7.49 billion in 1995.
Sweden, Denmark and Norway will also have well developed direct insurance markets by 2000, with France, Spain and Italy beginning to diversify beyond direct motor around the turn of the century.
Intermediaries such as brokers will retain a strong grip on markets in France, Germany and Italy, but the size of these markets will make them viable for direct insurers after 2000, Datamonitor said.
